#!/bin/bash

# find_hosts.sh - Ping sweep to find active hosts in a subnet

# Default subnet to scan (can be overridden by command line argument)
SUBNET="${1:-192.168.1.0}"

# Extract network prefix (e.g., 192.168.1 from 192.168.1.0)
NETWORK_PREFIX=$(echo "$SUBNET" | cut -d'.' -f1-3)

# Check if we need sudo for ping (on some systems)
if ! ping -c 1 -W 1 127.0.0.1 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    SUDO="sudo"
else
    SUDO=""
fi

echo "Scanning subnet: ${NETWORK_PREFIX}.*"

# Array to store active hosts
ACTIVE_HOSTS=()

# Perform ping sweep (skip network and broadcast addresses)
for i in {1..254}; do
    IP="${NETWORK_PREFIX}.${i}"
    
    # Use ping with minimal packets and timeout
    if $SUDO ping -c 1 -W 1 "$IP" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Host found: $IP"
        ACTIVE_HOSTS+="$IP "
    fi
    
    # Optional: Show progress
    if [ $i -eq 25 ] || [ $i -eq 50 ] || [ $i -eq 100 ] || [ $i -eq 200 ]; then
        echo "Progress: $i/254" >&2
    fi
done

# Summary
echo "\n=== Scan Complete ==="
if [ ${#ACTIVE_HOSTS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "No active hosts found."
else
    echo "Found ${#ACTIVE_HOSTS[@]} active host(s):"
    for host in ${ACTIVE_HOSTS[@]}; do
        echo "  $host"
    done
fi

exit 0

else

fi
